question.problem:
The duration of feline pregnancies is normally distributed with a mean of $\mu $ days and a standard deviation of $5$ days. Additionally, $20%$ of the pregnancies have a duration lower than $59$ days. Find the mean $\mu $, rounded to the nearest day.

*Hint: A table of values of ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ for different values of $p$ is given below, where $p=Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $p$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.10\,$ | $\,0.15\,$ | $\,0.20\,$ | $\,0.25\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ | $\,-2.3263\,$ | $\,-1.8808\,$ | $\,-1.6449\,$ | $\,-1.2816\,$ | $\,-1.0364\,$ | $\,-0.8416\,$ | $\,-0.6745\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the duration of a randomly selected pregnancy. Then we have $X∼N(\mu ,{5}^{2}),$ and we want to find the mean $\mu .$ 

We know that $P(X<59)=0.20.$ Converting $X$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<59) & =0.20 \\ P(Z\le \frac{59-\mu }{5}) & =0.20 \\ Φ(\frac{59-\mu }{5}) & =0.20 \\ \frac{59-\mu }{5} & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.20).\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, 

$$
{Φ}^{-1}(0.20)=-0.8416.
$$

Finally then, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{59-\mu }{5} & =-0.8416 \\ 59-\mu  & =-4.208 \\ \mu  & ≈63\,\text{days.}\end{aligned}
$$
